pageCache.pageTitle: Independent Prep School & Nursery in Richmond | Ages 3-11 | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
A welcome from our Headteacher
Welcome to Unicorn School, a thriving and academically ambitious community, founded in 1970 by a visionary group of local parents and teachers. From the very beginning, the aim was not simply to educate, but to create an environment in which children could flourish intellectually and creatively, developing a genuine love of learning that endures well beyond their prep years.
A broad and creative education
We pride ourselves in preparing children for the ever-changing world ahead, cultivating not just academic prowess, but also confidence, resilience, adaptability, and the lasting virtues of kindness and compassion. We want them to think independently and creatively and not to be afraid of making mistakes along the way.
Celebrating individual strengths
Unicorn is not just a place for academic excellence, but a vibrant hub of extra-curricular and enrichment activities for every child. From varied sports programs to arts and music sessions, our diverse range of activities aims to nurture well-rounded individuals. Rock band, virtual reality, chess, karate, cookery, Unicorn singers, dance, pottery, golf, padel, riding and sailing are just a few of the exciting opportunities awaiting your child.
A kind, caring family feel
We place an emphasis on the importance of building a sense of community, teaching children to appreciate diversity, and instilling values that promote compassion, empathy and respect.
For children to thrive both inside and outside the classroom, they need to know they matter and that they are fully supported. At Unicorn, the pastoral care and wellbeing of the children is our utmost priority. We provide a warm and nurturing environment along with the excellent relationships between children and staff which means that no child is in any doubt the staff here will lend a safe and sympathetic ear whenever they may need it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s welcome | Prep School South West London | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Unicorn School, a thriving and academically ambitious community, founded in 1970 by a visionary group of local parents and teachers. From the very beginning, the aim was not simply to educate, but to create an environment in which children could flourish intellectually and creatively, developing a genuine love of learning that endures well beyond their prep years.
That founding vision remains at the heart of the school today. Our curriculum is both rigorous and forward-thinking, carefully designed to challenge and inspire. We place a strong emphasis on academic depth and breadth, encouraging pupils to think critically, question confidently and engage with ideas at a meaningful level. Supported by a highly skilled and dedicated staff, each child is individually known and guided to discover their particular strengths, interests and intellectual potential.
At Unicorn, academic excellence sits alongside a deep commitment to character education. We strive to cultivate not only capable learners, but thoughtful, resilient and compassionate individuals. In the Early Years and Infants, we lay firm foundations through a rich, play-informed approach that fosters curiosity, language development and early reasoning skills. As pupils progress into the Juniors, this develops into a more explicit culture of enquiry, supported by disciplines such as philosophy, reasoning and “brain-time”, which nurture analytical thinking and intellectual independence. This balanced and academically ambitious approach is reflected in our excellent outcomes across academic subjects, the arts and sport, and in the wide range of highly regarded senior schools to which our pupils move on.
Unicorn is both successful and vibrant, underpinned by attentive and proactive pastoral care that ensures every child feels secure and valued. As we prepare our pupils for an increasingly complex and fast-changing world, we equip them not only with strong academic foundations, but with the confidence, adaptability and moral integrity they will need to thrive.
I warmly invite you to visit and experience, first-hand, the energy, warmth and magic that is Unicorn School.
Polly Fraley Headteacher
“Still, words like unicorn and rainbow can be misleading – this is not a fluffy, cuddly academic vacuum, but a serious place of learning and development.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and aims | Nursery in Richmond | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
Our ethos
We are a close-knit community full of happy, enthusiastic children where kindness is a key value and talked about every day. The intentions of the school’s founders remain at the forefront of our rationale. This is to be a forward-thinking school that educates children without unnecessary pressure, encouraging them to flourish both academically and creatively whilst enjoying the process of learning. Children leave us interested in the world around them and excited to embrace new challenges.
The Unicorn Code
We also have a Unicorn Code, which is reviewed annually by the children on the School Council together with Mrs Fraley.
Our aims
“Still, words like unicorn and rainbow can be misleading – this is not a fluffy, cuddly academic vacuum, but a serious place of learning and development.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Thursday clubs | Prep Schools Richmond | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
Unusually for a primary school setting, we dedicate Thursday afternoons exclusively to extra-curricular opportunities for our Junior pupils. During this time, children step away from their usual curriculum lessons and immerse themselves in a broad and enriching programme of activities. These sessions are carefully designed to nurture curiosity, build confidence, and allow children to explore and develop a wide range of interests, talents, and new skills.
Our Thursday afternoon provision ensures that every child has the opportunity to discover something new, collaborate with different peers, and engage in experiences that support both their personal and social development. The clubs are varied and inclusive, catering to a wide spectrum of interests and abilities, and are led by enthusiastic staff who are passionate about their subjects.
Thursday afternoon clubs include:
We also run activity clubs during and after school. These clubs include Karate, Musical Theatre, Swimming, Chess, Virtual Reality, M:tech (music technology), Sew what?, Unicorn Singers, La Jolie Ronde French Club, School of Comedy and Little Voices.
The Good Schools Guide
“Produces considerate and thoughtful children, we sensed. We were struck by natural, inherent good manners.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Arts week | Richmond Prep Schools | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
Arts Week takes place annually in the spring term. In recent years the children have enjoyed the following themes:
2025 – Madagascar
Another action-packed week as the whole school studied Madagascar. Classes learnt all about the extraordinary range of flora and fauna, the wide variety of habitats and ecosystems, whilst also debating the issues of poverty on the island, the effects of deforestation and how different life is like in an equatorial country. Lessons have included plotting graphs comparing rainfall in different habitats on the island, reading stories from and about Madagascar, creating moving chameleon sculptures and beautiful glass paintings, and making vanilla ice cream.
Learning all about the unique and often bizarre ways that animals have evolved on the island has been a particular delight, from studying leaping ring tailed lemurs to the long-fingered aye-aye, as well as the spiky tenrec and the predatory fossa. All classes attended some brilliant workshops seeing many examples of the wonders of Madagascan plant life, which really brought to life all that the classes had learnt in their lessons at school.
2024 - Sustainability
2023 – Japan – Konnichiwa!
Year 6 playing the big drums of Japan
2022 – Maths in Art and Nature
2020 – Conference of the birds

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative Arts | Prep School in Kew, Richmond | Unicorn School
pageCache.text:
Lessons in art and design technology and drama are linked to class projects and throughout the school there is an abundance of creative, colourful artwork displayed. As well as class music lessons, children can enjoy singing lessons and learn from a choice of ten or so different instruments.
“Unicorn School is friendly, fun and creatively stimulating with a really caring ethos”.
